newsitem.title: INDIA: GOLD-Indian sub-continent prices seen rising.
newsitem.headline: GOLD-Indian sub-continent prices seen rising.

text.p: Gold prices are expected to rise further in the Indian sub-continent, powered by demand sparked by a recent downtrend in world markets, dealers said on Monday.
On the Bombay bullion market, gold gained 110 rupees to 4,565 rupees in the week to Monday, for a rise of 215 rupees per 10 grammes in the past fortnight.
In Pakistan, gold prices are likely to remain mixed but had begun picking up from low levels, dealers said.
Demand for gold jewellery was quite low, they said.
In Dubai, the re-export market for the sub-continent, traders said demand received support from Indian orders.
"Domestic gold had also received help from a recovery in world markets though prices abroad still ruled relatively lower," said Babubhai Jain, a leading Bombay dealer.
Jain said firming premium on special import licences that needed to import gold also helped market sentiment. The premium rose to 13.00 percent from 12.00 percent a week ago.

"Physical buying may remain low this month but will pick up in August ahead of Hindu festivals," he said. The four-month Hindu festival season which begins next month is expected to generate demand for gold.
Traders in the Gulf business hub of Dubai said rising bullion prices had taken the shine off the local retail market which had seen turnover pick up this month on gold's slump to 12-year price lows.

Re-exports to India were also dulled by the monsoon season though levels remained supported by some Indian importers advancing their orders from August because of the recent downturn in prices, traders and wholesalers said.
"July has seen some good buying in the local market and into India but this has slowed because of the turnround in gold prices," said an Indian expatriate trader based in Dubai.
